answer.evidence: The score-to-grade mapping is `mi_rank` at radon/metrics.py:150-157. It returns `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. The docstring says A for score > 19, B for 9 < score <= 19, and C for score <= 9. Both boundaries are inclusive on the lower grade. A score of exactly 9 gives C, and exactly 19 gives B. This matches the docstring. The boolean-arithmetic trick is easy to misread, so the boundary tests deserve a close look. I would check the rank against 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01. The rank-boundary logic in radon/complexity.py:15 (`cc_rank`) is the closest comparison point, so I would check its threshold style against `mi_rank`. radon/raw.py supplies the LOC and comment counts that feed the MI input, so I would check that those inputs are not skewed. radon/visitors.py only feeds the Halstead and complexity inputs, so it gets a short pass.
